title: qa-regression regression.json — classified build + unit-test gate verdict
description: The ratified output of the qa-regression skill, written to <evid_root>/<key>/regression.json. The recipe/router branches on `status` and `next_action`. HARD RULE (QA-REGRESSION-C1): status 'green' / next_action 'ship-ok' require results.total >= 1 and a non-empty area_slice_run — a zero-test run must emit blocked-slice-empty (the incident shape: area_slice_run [] + total 'n/a' + ship-ok, which once shipped a real PR). contracts/validate.py enforces that rule on every regression.json, and results counts are INTEGERS, so 'n/a' fails validation by design. v1.1.0 (additive): OPTIONAL `flakiness_writes` — a flakiness data point is written for EVERY test run, not only for a flip, because a rate computed only from flips is not a rate and the R7 quarantine threshold reads it. v2.0.0 (BREAKING): the Playwright browser-suite slice is gone — this gate drives no browser and runs no spec files. The gate is build + lint against the pre-fix baseline + the unit tests covering the fixed area + the full unit suite of every changed project. Removed: status 'drift', next_action 'heal', failed_specs class 'drift' (there is no selector healing lane), and the `preflight` key (its script was deleted).

status.description: Worst-class-wins verdict. blocked-environment = the test runner or its dependencies broke (NOT blast radius); blocked-slice-empty = zero tests selected/executed for the area (never ship-ok).

next_action.description: What the recipe should do. ship-ok is only legal with status green AND results.total >= 1.

area.description: The derived area whose tests ran.

area_slice_run.description: Test files actually run for the fixed area. Empty + status green is a contract lie — validate.py rejects it.

smoke_slice_run.description: The broader runs that catch blast radius — the full unit suite of each changed project (e.g. 'web unit suite (full)', 'api unit suite (full)' — one per conventions.projects[] entry touched).

spec.description: The failing test, as '<test file> > <test name>'.

flakiness_writes.description: OPTIONAL (v1.1.0). How many flakiness rows this run wrote to the brain — one `kb write flakiness --spec <s> [--failed]` per test RUN, pass or fail. Writing only on a flip makes flake_rate = failures/runs meaningless (every recorded run would be a failure), and R7's quarantine threshold in .claude/loops/loop-limits.json reads that rate. So on a healthy run this equals results.total; it is lower only when a test ran but the write was refused or queued (see the kb outbox). Cross-checkable against `kb receipt --ticket <KEY>` via `contracts/validate.py --receipts`. Key absent = pre-v1.1.0 artifact, NOT 'wrote none'.

baseline.description: lint_before comes from dev-fix's lint-baseline.json (the declared producer); when that file is absent set baseline_missing:true and never invent a baseline.

detail.description: OPTIONAL: human-readable blocking detail on blocked-* statuses (e.g. what the area test search looked for).

attempt.description: OPTIONAL (v2.1.0). Which attempt of this stage produced the artifact, 1-based. Added because the retry audit had to be reconstructed from session transcripts — no artifact recorded its own attempt number, so a retry was indistinguishable from a first pass after the fact. A retry requires transient-failure evidence; a deterministic failure escalates or changes strategy instead of repeating.

retry_reason.description: OPTIONAL (v2.1.0). Why this attempt happened, when attempt > 1 — the flaky-store match, infra error, timeout or oracle exit 2 that justified it.

timing.description: OPTIONAL (v2.1.0). When this stage ran. Costs microseconds to write and is the only way to tell whether a pipeline redesign still holds months later — without it every duration has to be reconstructed from session transcripts, which do not always exist.
